answer: Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the zenith forfeiture shows up in the ocean totals with the grove audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 182 aliases after a single epoch thus destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. Retiring an identity early forfeits 29% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
